.
CEDA dates back to the early 2000s when Sangwon Suh developed it initially at Leiden University and later at the University of Minnesota

. It was initially a US single-region model accompanied by environmental extensions to report many environmental indicators. It was maintained an applied by the company VitalMetrics for private, public and academic applications. It was expanded to become a global MRIO model focused on GHG emissions before Watershed acquired it in 2023 and GHG emission factors for Scope 3 reporting became its primary purpose, releasing an free version of emissions factors as openCEDA in 2024.
USEEIO was a research product of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) first released in early 2017  and developed as fully open-source model
. USEEIO built off the contributions of earlier US single-region EEIO models including the Carnegie Mellon EIO-LCA model
, and CEDA, and primary versions include v1 and v2.0

were used for multi-indicator assessments.
USEEIO was initially developed for applications of the USEPA’s Sustainable Materials Management program. Beginning in 2020 the Supply Chain GHG Emission Factors were created from USEEIO for Scope 3 reporting, initially at the request of the EPA Center for Corporate Climate Leadership and later continued at the request of the White House Office of Sustainability and the General Services Administration

and became the most popular use of the model and one of the USEPA’s most popular open source datasets.
The limitations of the single-region for modeling consumption impacts in the U.S. were addressed in late v2 models by coupling them with global MRIO models

.
The USEPA ceased updating the USEEIO model in 2025.
A primary motivation for the formation of the Cornerstone Sustainability Data Initiative (Cornerstone) was to continue maintaining the USEEIO model and to bring it together with CEDA.

of Cornerstone EEIO is in 2026, the model is only “new” in the sense of the reconciliation of the methods behind USEEIO and CEDA, major methodological innovations
including ABSR and nowcasting US tables that have been added (see a complete list under Releases), and assembly through a new data pipeline.
